newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel told to be calm despite Gulf tension.
newsitem.headline: Israel told to be calm despite Gulf tension.

text.p: Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai said on Friday the Jewish state should continue life as usual despite tensions over a possible U.S. attack on Iraq.
"We don't think we have to have any connection or involvement in the process itself," Mordechai told Israel Television.
"Life should continue as is in the State of Israel," he said as Israelis immersed themselves in the start of the Jewish New Year, which runs through Sunday.
Iraq fired 39 Scud missiles at Israel during the 1991 Gulf War.
U.S. warplanes and a second aircraft carrier converged on the Gulf on Friday in readiness to punish Iraqi President Saddam Hussein for shooting at Western patrols of no-fly zones over Iraq.
However, Baghdad later said it was suspending its threat to shoot at aircraft policing a five-year-old ban on Iraqi flights over the north or south of Iraq.
